Updating rsyncrosim scripts to version 2

Source: vignettes/a07_updating_rsyncrosim_scripts_to_v2.Rmd
a07_updating_rsyncrosim_scripts_to_v2.Rmd

The introduction of SyncroSim Studio brought some structural changes and new features, which are reflected in the rsyncrosim package. Use the guide below to update your rsyncrosim version 1 scripts to be compatible with version 2.

Note: SyncroSim v3.0.9 or higher is required to use rsyncrosim v2.0.0 or higher.

Updated functions

Installing/uninstalling packages

Previously, the addPackage and removePackage functions were used to install and uninstall packages from SyncroSim. Now to install and uninstall packages from SyncroSim, use:

installPackage()   # Installs the selected package(s) to SyncroSim
uninstallPackage() # Uninstalls the selected package(s) from SyncroSim

Adding/removing packages

Now you can use multiple SyncroSim packages in a single library. To add and remove packages from your library, use:

addPackage()    # Adds package(s) to the library
removePackage() # Removes package(s) from the library.

Note that when you remove a package from your library any associated datasheets will be removed as well.

Deprecated functions

In SyncroSim 3, the concept of addon packages no longer exists. All addon packages have either been converted to standalone packages (e.g., burnP3PlusPrometheus), and can be added to a library without having to load a base package first, or incorporated directly into the base packages (e.g., stsimsf is now part of stsim). Therefore, the following functions have been removed:

addon()
disableAddon()
enableAddon()

datasheetRaster() # previously deprecated function. Use datasheetSpatRaster() instead.

addBreakpoint()
breakpoint()
deleteBreakpoint()

ssimUpdate()
updatePackage()

Library

Given this added flexibility, the addon argument has been removed from the ssimLibrary() function, and the package argument has been renamed to packages.

# instead of using
myLibrary <- ssimLibrary(package = "PackageName", addon = "AddonName")

# use
myLibrary <- ssimLibrary(packages = c("stsim", "helloworldSpatial"))
## Package <stsim v4.0.1> added
## Package <helloworldSpatial v2.0.0> added

info(ssimLibrary) no longer shows the Package name, Current package version and Minimum package version, and the Input and Output folder paths have been combined into the Data folder. See the Introduction to rsyncrosim for details.

The template and addon arguments have also been removed. You can download template libraries from SyncroSim Cloud.

Dependencies

To view the existing dependencies for a scenario, use:

dependency(myScenario)
##   ScenarioId       Name Priority
## 1          1 Scenario 1        1

To set dependencies for a scenario:

# Change from:
dependency(myScenario, dependency = c("Scenario 2", "Scenario 3"))
# To:
dependency(myScenario) <- c("Scenario 2", "Scenario 3")

dependency(myScenario)
##   ScenarioId       Name Priority
## 1          2 Scenario 2        1
## 2          3 Scenario 3        2

Note that this will remove any previously set dependencies unless the existing dependencies are also included in the vector. Also, the order in which the dependencies are listed can be important. In this example, Scenario 2 takes precedence over Scenario 3.

Multiprocessing

The run() function no longer has the jobs argument. Use the core_Multiprocessing library datasheet to set the number of cores to use. Note that this will affect every scenario run.

multiprocessing <-
    data.frame(EnableMultiprocessing = TRUE,
               MaximumJobs = 6,
               EnableMultiScenario = TRUE) # optional, to run multiple scenarios in parallel
  
saveDatasheet(myLibrary, multiprocessing, "core_Multiprocessing")

Variable naming

The ID in the primary key changed to Id for all datasheets. That also means that the column names for variables depending on higher-level datasheets also changed their suffixes to Id. It is generally safe to substitute ID for Id throughout your script, but it’s recommended to check the datasheet’s variable names.

datasheet(myScenario, "stsim_FlowPathway", includeKey = TRUE, optional = TRUE, empty = TRUE)
##  [1] FlowPathwayId                Iteration                   
##  [3] Timestep                     FromStratumId               
##  [5] FromSecondaryStratumId       FromTertiaryStratumId       
##  [7] FromStateClassId             FromAgeMin                  
##  [9] FromStockTypeId              ToStratumId                 
## [11] ToStateClassId               ToAgeMin                    
## [13] ToStockTypeId                TransitionGroupId           
## [15] StateAttributeTypeId         FlowTypeId                  
## [17] TargetType                   Multiplier                  
## [19] TransferToStratumId          TransferToSecondaryStratumId
## [21] TransferToTertiaryStratumId  TransferToStateClassId      
## [23] TransferToAgeMin            
## <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

Core datasheets

The system datasheets, previously identified by corestime_, are now simply called core_.

Other NEW functions 

createCondaEnv(pkgs = c()) # creates the conda environment for the selected package(s)

deleteLibrary() # Note this is irreversible

chart() # Create or load a SyncroSim chart. Explore other charting functions with ?chart
